items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: I went down to Wispering Pines with Doc Cheatham and Red Richards and Herb Hall and we made another album while we

ctx.x: I don't know whether that many people heard it not. I have not heard any reaction from the album. I don't think that these guys actually worked together except on that particular date. Because Herb Hall and Doc Cheatham and Marshall, they're all on their own. And, of course, there were a lot of other young musicians on the session that day. They did other tunes which way over my head. They were way out!

items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: You did an album with Beaver Harris, where Maxine Sullivan is on the same album with you. An Album called, 'From Ragtime to No Time.' ... Right.

ctx.x: Definitely were few. He never had an opportunity, I don't think. That he should've had. He died too early, came along a little too early, I think.

But getting back to 1940 and well, you recorded then in '41, I know with Benny Carter, Vic Dickenson, Archy Archie, Sidney Sydney DeParis and I think Maxine Sullivan was the vocalist, I guess she was big then?
